extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, academics, and professionals seeking jobs, scholarships, prizes, courses, and society notices
extracted.subtask_description: Announcements and notices of academic posts, scholarships, prizes, and courses, giving eligibility, application requirements, deadlines, and other conditions for applicants and competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRAHAM SCHOLARSHIP in Pathology — application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications addressed to the Principal Officer, University of London, South Kensington, S.W.7, must (a2) be accompanied by the names of not more than three references, one at least of which should be the name of some Professor, Lecturer, or Teacher of the University or College in which the Candidate has conducted his studies in Pathology, (4) state the research upon which the applicant proposes to work, and (c) be received nor later than the first post on Monday January 1, 1923. Envelopes should be marked 'GRAHAM SCHOLARSHIP.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scholarship enables a young man to continue pathological researches and to secure his services to the School of Advanced Medical Studies connected with University College Hospital as a Teacher under the direction of the Professor of Pathology. The successful candidate will be expected to take up the Scholarship as from April 1, 1923. The Scholarship is in no way restricted to students either of University College Hospital Medical School or any other Medical School of the University of London. Intending applicants may call personally on the Professor for fuller information after appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRAHAM SCHOLARSHIP — eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The GRAHAM SCHOLARSHIP in PATHOLOGY, value £300 per annum for two years, founded under the will of the late Dr. Charles Graham to enable young man to continue his pathological researches and at the same time to secure his services to the School of Advanced Medical Studies connected with University College Hospital as a Teacher under the direction of the Professor of Pathology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not restricted to students of particular medical schools; may be held subject to the conditions described (start date April 1, 1923).

rubrics_metrics.name: CECIL MEDAL and Prize — topic and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The CECIL MEDAL and PRIZE of £10 will be awarded in May 1923 for the best Paper on 'Recent Advances in Chemistry as applied to Agriculture, with special reference to Dorset conditions.' Open to Persons aged 17-35, born in Dorset or resident One Year between May 1, 1921 and 1923.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must meet age and birthplace/residence requirements and submit a paper on the specified subject; particulars obtainable from Mr. H. Pouncy, Dorchester.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Cape Town — Senior Lectureship in Physiology — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited for the POST of SENIOR LECTURER in the DEPARTMENT of PHYSIOLOGY at a salary of £450 per annum rising by annual increments of £25 to a maximum of £650 per annum. (The successful applicant, if a qualified medical practitioner, will be allowed a salary of £500 for the first three years of his appointment.) An allowance of £40 will be made for passage money. The lecturer must become a member of the University Teachers’ Superannuation Fund. The successful applicant will be expected to assume duty on March 12, 1923, or as soon thereafter as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and copies of testimonials, all in duplicate, must reach the SECRETARY, Office of the High Commissioner for the Union of South Africa, Trafalgar Square, W.C., not later than January 31, 1923. Forms of Application and further particulars may be obtained from the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: University College, London — Assistant Lecturer in Physical Chemistry — application materials and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, accompanied by testimonials, record of degree or degrees obtained, published work, and teaching experience (if any), are invited for the above post. Salary £300 per annum. Physicists who possess a knowledge of Chemistry, as well as Chemists, are eligible for the post. Applications to be sent as soon as possible, and not later than December 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should include evidence of qualifications (degrees), publications, and any teaching experience; further particulars from the Secretary, University College, London.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harper Adams Agricultural College — Advisory Mycologist — application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited for the post of ADVISORY MYCOLOGIST. Particulars of the appointment may be obtained on application to the Principal, to whom all applications, together with copies of three recent testimonials, should be addressed not later than December 18, 1922.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit particulars and three recent testimonials by the stated deadline; obtain particulars from Principal beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: University of Leeds — Additional Instructor in Horticulture — application deadline and salary
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited for the position of additional INSTRUCTOR in HORTICULTURE. Salary £230. Applications will be received up to December 20, 1922, and should be addressed to the REGISTRAR, The University, Leeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should request further particulars from the Registrar; include usual application materials (not specified on page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal of the Textile Institute — editorial applicant qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: WANTED, for editorial office of the JOURNAL OF THE TEXTILE INSTITUTE, young man trained in science and with literary ability, to take up duties immediately with a view to appointment as Editor; full-time service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should state qualifications (including modern languages), and commencing salary, to GENERAL SECRETARY, Textile Institute, 16 St. Mary’s Parsonage, Manchester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sir John Cass Technical Institute — Mathematical Theory and Applications of Statistics course suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: A Course of Ten Lectures on the modern mathematical methods of dealing with statistical data in social, educational, economic, meteorological and medical problems, suitable to teachers and to students of economics, meteorology and medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities will be given to students who wish to undertake special investigations and research work associated with the course; lectures Fridays from 7 to 9 P.M.; first lecture January 12, 1923; detailed syllabus available on application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sir John Cass Technical Institute — Alternating Currents and Electrical Oscillations course suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: A Course of Ten Lectures accompanied by Practical Demonstrations, and intended for post-graduate students and those otherwise qualified to pursue this branch of electrical science and its applications in wireless telegraphy and telephony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tuesdays from 7 to 8.30 P.M.; first lecture January 9, 1923; detailed syllabus available on application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural norms in notices (general pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Across multiple notices: applicants are expected to send testimonials/references, records of degrees, published work, and state proposed research or qualifications; applications must be sent by specified deadlines and to named officers/addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many notices require duplicates of testimonials, specified envelope markings (e.g., 'GRAHAM SCHOLARSHIP'), and that further particulars be requested from named officials. Meeting stated deadlines and including the requested supporting documents are explicit requirements for consideration.
